newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-FOUR SHARE LEAD IN OHIO TOURNAMENT AFTER FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FOUR SHARE LEAD IN OHIO TOURNAMENT AFTER FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Four players shared the
first-round lead at six under par after the first round of the
$1.9 million Memorial Tournament on Thursday.
Sweden's Jesper Parnevik, Tim Herron, Billy Andrade and
Glen Day shot rounds of 66 at Muirfield Village.
Scott Hoch was a stroke behind at 67.
Masters champion and overall sensation Tiger Woods shot an
opening-round par 72.
Woods appeared to be on the way to his worst round of the
year, three over par after 12 holes. But a good finish brought
him back par.
Woods sank a 25 foot putt for eagle on the par five 15th
hole, then made a 12 footer on the next hole for birdie.
Despite recovering at the end, Woods was not particularly
happy with his play. "It was army golf. I was left, right,
left, right all day. I also had 'liprosy.' I must have left
five putts on the lip today," Woods said.
Tournament host Jack Nicklaus had his best opening round
at Muirfield since 1986. A bogey on the last hole left him in
ninth place at three under par 69.
"I didn't expect to shoot a good round today, although I
felt like I was playing fairly decently. I just haven't played
in so darn long, it's been six weeks since I played. What I
can do after this, I don't know.
"I feel it's awful hard for me to compete against these
kids anymore, but you never know," said the 57-year-old
Nicklaus.
Parnevik's hopes of scoring well may have been even lower
than Nicklaus' on Thursday.
Parnevik, who has four second-place finishes in the U.S.
this year, went to Europe for the first time last week,
missing the cut at the Volvo PGA Championship. "Last week I
probably played the worst since I turned pro, so I came here
with no real expectations.
"I was actually pleased to be just one over after three
holes. But when the balls started to drop, all of a sudden
your confidence is back and it gets a lot easier to play,"
said Parnevik.
Both Herron and Andrade bogeyed the 18th hole to lose solo
posession of the lead. Herron had three bogeys, seven birdies
and an eagle in his round.
Herron defeated Woods 6&4 here in the second round of
matchplay at the 1992 U.S. Amateur. It was one of only two
defeats for Woods in the Amateur.
